definitionEn: corals turning white because of heat stress.
meaningVi: hiện tượng san hô bị tẩy trắng
existingExample: Rising sea temperatures cause mass coral bleaching.

definitionEn: the falling pH of the oceans as they absorb carbon dioxide.
existingExample: Ocean acidification makes it harder for shellfish to build shells.

definitionEn: a series of organisms in which each is eaten by the next.
existingExample: Microplastics can enter the food chain through fish.

definitionEn: tiny pieces of plastic in the environment.
existingExample: Microplastics have been found in drinking water.

definitionEn: discarded electronic devices.
existingExample: Much e-waste is shipped to developing countries.

definitionEn: turning waste materials into products of higher value.
existingExample: Upcycling turns old furniture into new designs.

definitionEn: an economy that reuses and recycles materials to cut waste.
existingExample: A circular economy keeps materials in use for as long as possible.

definitionEn: a habit of discarding things rather than reusing or repairing them.
existingExample: Cheap fashion fuels a throwaway culture.

definitionEn: cheap clothes produced quickly to follow trends.
existingExample: Fast fashion generates huge amounts of textile waste.

definitionEn: misleading claims that a product is environmentally friendly.
meaningVi: tẩy xanh (quảng cáo xanh giả tạo)
existingExample: Regulators are cracking down on greenwashing.

definitionEn: aware of and concerned about the environment.
meaningVi: có ý thức bảo vệ môi trường
existingExample: Environmentally conscious consumers choose reusable products.

definitionEn: the point at which a small change causes a large, irreversible effect.
meaningVi: điểm tới hạn (không thể đảo ngược)
existingExample: Scientists fear the Amazon rainforest could reach a tipping point.

definitionEn: causing great damage or suffering.
existingExample: Unchecked warming could have catastrophic consequences.

definitionEn: to destroy or badly damage something.
existingExample: The cyclone devastated coastal villages.

definitionEn: easily harmed or affected.
existingExample: Small island nations are especially vulnerable to rising seas.

definitionEn: responsible care for the natural environment.
meaningVi: trách nhiệm gìn giữ môi trường
existingExample: Indigenous communities often practise careful environmental stewardship.

definitionEn: that must be obeyed by law.
meaningVi: có hiệu lực ràng buộc pháp lý
existingExample: Countries signed a legally binding agreement to cut emissions.

definitionEn: a system in which companies buy and sell permits to emit greenhouse gases.
meaningVi: mua bán hạn ngạch phát thải
existingExample: The EU runs an emissions trading scheme for heavy industry.

definitionEn: the principle that those who cause pollution should pay for it.
meaningVi: nguyên tắc người gây ô nhiễm phải trả tiền
existingExample: Under the polluter pays principle, factories fund the clean-up.

definitionEn: a study of how a project will affect the environment.
meaningVi: đánh giá tác động môi trường
existingExample: Large infrastructure projects require an environmental impact assessment.

definitionEn: a person who works to protect nature.
existingExample: Conservationists warn that the species could vanish within a decade.

definitionEn: tourism that supports conservation and benefits local people.
existingExample: Eco-tourism can fund the protection of rainforests.

definitionEn: an area where wildlife and plants are protected.
existingExample: The wetland was declared a nature reserve.

definitionEn: a non-native species that spreads and harms local wildlife.
existingExample: Invasive species can wipe out native plants.

definitionEn: originating naturally in a particular place.
existingExample: Indigenous plants are better adapted to local conditions.

definitionEn: a chemical used to kill insects that damage crops.
existingExample: Some pesticides have been linked to declining bee populations.

definitionEn: farming without artificial chemicals.
existingExample: Organic farming avoids synthetic pesticides.

definitionEn: growing a single crop over a large area.
existingExample: Monocultures make crops vulnerable to disease.

definitionEn: to fill something up again.
existingExample: Heavy rains help replenish underground water supplies.

definitionEn: water held underground in soil or rock.
existingExample: Over-pumping has caused groundwater levels to fall.

definitionEn: to control and use natural forces.
existingExample: Countries are learning to harness the power of the sun.

definitionEn: planting trees where there was no forest before.
existingExample: Afforestation schemes can help absorb carbon dioxide.

definitionEn: a scientist who studies living things and their environment.
existingExample: Ecologists study how species interact within ecosystems.

definitionEn: a city area that is significantly warmer than the countryside around it.
existingExample: Dark roads and concrete buildings intensify the urban heat island effect.

definitionEn: to reduce or stop the effect of something by doing something that works against it.
existingExample: Regular exercise can help counteract the effects of sitting all day.

definitionEn: expected or predicted to happen.
existingExample: The cooling effect turned out to be larger than anticipated.

definitionEn: the process by which plants release water vapour through their leaves.
meaningVi: sự thoát hơi nước (ở lá cây)
existingExample: Trees cool their surroundings partly through transpiration.

definitionEn: the layer of branches and leaves formed by the tops of trees.
existingExample: Neighbourhoods with more canopy cover stay cooler in summer.

definitionEn: increasing rapidly in amount, intensity or seriousness.
existingExample: Escalating housing costs are pushing young families out of city centres.

definitionEn: to balance one effect with an opposite one.
existingExample: Planting forests can only partly offset carbon emissions.

definitionEn: needing a lot of effort, money or time to succeed.
meaningVi: đầy tham vọng, quy mô lớn
existingExample: The city launched an ambitious programme to plant a million trees.

definitionEn: having a mild climate that is neither very hot nor very cold.
existingExample: Trees grow quickly in temperate regions with regular rainfall.

definitionEn: containing a lot of water vapour in the air.
existingExample: Hot and humid weather makes physical work exhausting.

definitionEn: Excessive enrichment of water bodies with nutrients, triggering dense algal blooms that deplete dissolved oxygen.
meaningVi: hiện tượng phú dưỡng nguồn nước gây thiếu oxy
existingExample: Unchecked agricultural fertiliser runoff has accelerated eutrophication across coastal estuaries, creating vast marine dead zones.

definitionEn: A thick subsurface layer of soil and rock that remains continuously frozen for two or more consecutive years.
meaningVi: tầng đất đóng băng vĩnh cửu vùng cực
existingExample: Thawing Arctic permafrost threatens to release billions of tonnes of trapped methane, amplifying global warming feedbacks.

definitionEn: A natural reservoir such as a forest, peatland, or ocean that absorbs more atmospheric carbon than it emits.
meaningVi: bể hấp thụ và lưu trữ carbon tự nhiên
existingExample: Preserving old-growth tropical rainforests is vital because they operate as an irreplaceable terrestrial carbon sink.

definitionEn: The proportion of incoming solar radiation reflected by a planetary surface, notably high over snow and ice.
meaningVi: suất phản chiếu bức xạ mặt trời của bề mặt Trái Đất
existingExample: As polar sea ice retreats, lower planetary albedo causes dark ocean water to absorb substantially more solar heat.

definitionEn: An underground layer of water-bearing permeable rock or unconsolidated material from which groundwater can be extracted.
existingExample: Intensive irrigation in semi-arid farming belts is pumping fossil water far faster than each deep aquifer can recharge.

definitionEn: An area of land that drains all streams and rainfall to a common river, basin, or coastal outlet.
meaningVi: lưu vực thoát nước, vùng đầu nguồn sông
existingExample: Restoring native vegetation along the upper watershed significantly reduces downstream flooding and sediment siltation.

definitionEn: The deliberate use of living microorganisms or plants to break down or neutralise hazardous environmental pollutants.
meaningVi: xử lý ô nhiễm bằng vi sinh vật và thực vật
existingExample: Following offshore oil spills, coastal authorities increasingly deploy bioremediation to degrade persistent hydrocarbons safely.

definitionEn: A sustainable land-use system that integrates trees and shrubs with crops or livestock on the same plot.
meaningVi: hệ thống canh tác nông lâm kết hợp
existingExample: Smallholders adopting agroforestry enjoy more stable harvests while simultaneously curbing topsoil erosion and boosting shade.

definitionEn: An agricultural design philosophy aiming to create self-sustaining ecosystems that mimic natural ecological patterns.
meaningVi: nông nghiệp bền vững mô phỏng hệ sinh thái tự nhiên
existingExample: Community farms built around permaculture principles minimise synthetic inputs by composting organic waste into fertile mulch.

definitionEn: Relating to or produced by the internal thermal energy stored beneath the Earth's crust.
meaningVi: thuộc về địa nhiệt (nhiệt lượng từ lòng đất)
existingExample: Unlike intermittent wind or solar arrays, geothermal power stations can supply steady baseload electricity around the clock.

definitionEn: Relating to the direct conversion of light radiation into electrical current using semiconductor materials.
meaningVi: thuộc quang điện (chuyển hóa trực tiếp ánh sáng thành điện năng)
existingExample: Dramatic price drops in photovoltaic panels have made rooftop solar generation economically viable for middle-income households.

definitionEn: Contaminated liquid that percolates through solid waste in a landfill and extracts dissolved toxic chemicals.
meaningVi: nước rỉ rác chứa chất độc hại từ bãi chôn lấp
existingExample: Modern sanitary landfills must install impermeable clay liners to prevent hazardous leachate from seeping into local rivers.

definitionEn: The gradual build-up of persistent chemical substances, such as mercury or pesticides, within a living organism over time.
meaningVi: sự tích tụ sinh học của độc tố trong cơ thể
existingExample: Marine biologists warn that the bioaccumulation of heavy metals in apex predatory fish poses serious risks to coastal diets.

definitionEn: Powerful indirect ecological interactions triggered when changes in apex predator populations ripple across lower food-web levels.
meaningVi: hiệu ứng dây chuyền qua các bậc dinh dưỡng
existingExample: Reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone sparked a remarkable trophic cascade that allowed riverside willow groves to regenerate.

definitionEn: An organism whose ecological role has a disproportionately large effect on maintaining the stability of its community.
meaningVi: loài chủ chốt duy trì cấu trúc toàn bộ hệ sinh thái
existingExample: Because sea otters restrain kelp-grazing urchins, losing this keystone species can rapidly collapse an entire underwater forest.

definitionEn: The division of large, continuous natural environments into smaller, isolated patches due to roads, farming, or construction.
meaningVi: sự phân mảnh sinh cảnh tự nhiên
existingExample: Motorways cutting through national parks accelerate habitat fragmentation, restricting gene flow among large mammals.

definitionEn: The gradual, predictable sequence of species composition changes as a biological community develops or recovers after disturbance.
meaningVi: quá trình diễn thế sinh thái tự nhiên
existingExample: Following a controlled wildfire, ecological succession allows pioneer grasses to stabilise soil before hardwood trees return.

definitionEn: The maximum population size or level of resource consumption an environment can sustain indefinitely without degrading.
meaningVi: sức chứa sinh thái tối đa của một môi trường
existingExample: Unregulated coastal tourism has pushed several Mediterranean islands well beyond their freshwater carrying capacity.

definitionEn: The accumulation of water-soluble salts in soil or freshwater bodies to levels that impair crop growth and ecosystems.
meaningVi: quá trình nhiễm mặn đất đai và nguồn nước ngọt
existingExample: Rising sea levels and upstream damming have intensified delta salinisation, threatening rice harvests for millions of farmers.

definitionEn: A long-term climatic shift toward progressively drier conditions that permanently reduces regional water availability.
meaningVi: quá trình khô hạn hóa dài hạn ở quy mô khu vực
existingExample: Hydrologists distinguish temporary droughts from structural aridification, which demands lasting redesign of municipal water grids.

definitionEn: The progressive shrinking of a glacier's terminus when annual ice melt consistently exceeds snowfall accumulation.
meaningVi: sự tan lùi và thu hẹp diện tích của sông băng
existingExample: Accelerated glacial retreat across the Himalayas jeopardises dry-season drinking water supplies for densely populated river basins.

definitionEn: The increase in volume of ocean water as it absorbs excess atmospheric heat, contributing directly to sea-level rise.
meaningVi: sự giãn nở nhiệt của khối nước đại dương
existingExample: Alongside melting polar ice sheets, oceanic thermal expansion accounts for nearly half of observed global sea-level rise.

definitionEn: Deliberate policies and technologies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions or enhancing carbon removal from the atmosphere.
meaningVi: các giải pháp giảm nhẹ biến đổi khí hậu tại nguồn
existingExample: Decarbonising heavy industry and electrifying freight fleets remain the twin pillars of credible national climate mitigation.

definitionEn: The capacity of communities, infrastructure, and ecosystems to anticipate, absorb, and recover from extreme climate shocks.
meaningVi: khả năng chống chịu và phục hồi trước biến đổi khí hậu
existingExample: Constructing sponge-city wetlands and flood-proof transit corridors strengthens urban climate resilience against erratic monsoons.

definitionEn: The removal or neutralisation of pollutants from contaminated soil, groundwater, or industrial sites to restore ecological safety.
meaningVi: công tác cải tạo và phục hồi môi trường ô nhiễm
existingExample: Before former mining zones can be converted into public parkland, developers must finance rigorous environmental remediation.

definitionEn: A biogeographic region that harbours exceptional concentrations of endemic species while facing acute habitat loss.
meaningVi: điểm nóng đa dạng sinh học đang bị đe dọa nghiêm trọng
existingExample: International conservation grants increasingly prioritise each tropical biodiversity hotspot where logging threatens undocumented flora.

definitionEn: Native to and exclusively restricted to a specific geographical area or isolated ecosystem.
existingExample: Invasive predators pose an existential threat to flightless birds that are endemic to remote oceanic islands.

definitionEn: Living in, inhabiting, or closely associated with trees and forest canopies.
meaningVi: thuộc về tán cây hoặc sinh sống chủ yếu trên cây
existingExample: Building rope bridges across forest clearings allows endangered arboreal primates to forage safely without descending to roads.

definitionEn: Relating to the open sea water column away from both the shoreline and the ocean floor.
meaningVi: thuộc vùng biển khơi xa bờ
existingExample: Establishing high-seas marine reserves is essential to safeguard migratory pelagic species from industrial drift-net fleets.

definitionEn: The industrial process of removing dissolved salts and minerals from seawater to produce potable freshwater.
meaningVi: quá trình khử muối biến nước biển thành nước ngọt
existingExample: While reverse-osmosis desalination secures drinking supplies in arid coastal states, disposing of hypersaline brine remains controversial.

definitionEn: The science and practice of controlling the establishment, growth, composition, and ecological health of forests.
existingExample: Selective-harvest silviculture balances commercial timber demand with the preservation of multi-layered woodland habitats.

definitionEn: The technological process of trapping carbon dioxide emissions at industrial sources or directly from ambient air for storage.
meaningVi: công nghệ thu giữ khí carbon từ nguồn phát thải
existingExample: Energy analysts caution that carbon capture should supplement rapid fossil-fuel phaseouts rather than excuse delayed action.

definitionEn: A state in which human demand for natural resources and waste absorption exceeds the biosphere's regenerative capacity.
meaningVi: tình trạng tiêu thụ tài nguyên vượt ngưỡng tái tạo sinh thái
existingExample: Shifting away from linear extraction is imperative if humanity intends to reverse decades of global ecological overshoot.

definitionEn: To completely destroy or eliminate a species or population from a particular geographic region.
meaningVi: xóa sổ hoàn toàn một loài khỏi một khu vực cụ thể
existingExample: Unchecked wetland drainage could extirpate rare amphibian populations from lowland floodplains within a single decade.

definitionEn: To strip a landscape or ecosystem of its natural resources, beauty, or ecological integrity through reckless exploitation.
existingExample: Strict mining moratoriums were enacted to prevent unlicensed corporations from continuing to despoil pristine alpine valleys.

definitionEn: To adapt physiologically or behaviourally to a new climate, altitude, or altered environmental regime.
meaningVi: thích nghi dần với điều kiện khí hậu hoặc môi trường mới
existingExample: Many cold-water coral reefs simply cannot acclimatise rapidly enough to survive consecutive marine heatwaves.

definitionEn: The proposed geological epoch characterised by pervasive human dominance over Earth's climate and biophysical systems.
existingExample: Environmental historians argue that surviving the anthropocene requires rethinking economic progress within planetary boundaries.

definitionEn: the newest and most advanced.
existingExample: The hospital has invested in cutting-edge diagnostic equipment.

definitionEn: the use of machines to do work that was previously done by people.
existingExample: Automation may replace many routine factory jobs in the coming decade.

definitionEn: no longer used because something newer exists.
existingExample: Smartphones have made many separate devices, such as cameras and maps, almost obsolete.

definitionEn: a new idea, method or invention.
existingExample: Governments can foster innovation by funding research in universities.

definitionEn: an important discovery that helps solve a problem.
existingExample: The new vaccine was hailed as a major medical breakthrough.

definitionEn: the gap between people who have access to modern technology and those who do not.
existingExample: Free public Wi-Fi could help bridge the digital divide between rich and poor.

definitionEn: easy for people to use or understand.
existingExample: The app's user-friendly design makes it popular among older people.

definitionEn: the protection of personal information from being misused.
existingExample: Many users are worried about how technology companies handle data privacy.

definitionEn: crime committed using computers or the internet.
existingExample: Banks are investing heavily to protect customers from cybercrime.

definitionEn: time spent using a phone, computer or television.
existingExample: Parents are advised to limit children's screen time before bed.

definitionEn: making you unable to stop doing or using something.
existingExample: Many apps are deliberately designed to be addictive.

definitionEn: the careful watching of people, especially by the police or government.
existingExample: Facial recognition technology has raised fears of mass surveillance.

definitionEn: working from home or from a place outside the office.
existingExample: Fast internet connections have made remote work possible for millions of people.

definitionEn: a small, useful machine or device.
meaningVi: thiết bị nhỏ, đồ công nghệ
existingExample: Teenagers often feel pressure to own the latest gadgets.

definitionEn: to improve a machine or system by adding newer parts.
existingExample: Companies must regularly upgrade their systems to stay secure.

definitionEn: the state of needing something too much.
existingExample: Our growing dependence on smartphones may weaken our memory.

definitionEn: false or inaccurate information that is spread.
existingExample: Social media platforms are under pressure to combat misinformation.

definitionEn: a set of rules that a computer follows to solve a problem.
existingExample: Recommendation algorithms decide much of what we watch online.

definitionEn: the ability to connect to the internet or to other devices.
existingExample: Rural areas still suffer from poor internet connectivity.

definitionEn: to change something completely and improve it.
existingExample: The internet has revolutionised the way people shop and communicate.
